subject: Audit log retention and export: chunked delivery & legal hold plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Lopez <alex.lopez@financio.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit log export: initial scope and constraints

Alex —

Quick follow-up from our call this morning. Financio asked for a copy of their tenant audit/access logs for the last 24 months, with delivery as a one-time handoff. A few practical constraints I want to call out up-front so we can set expectations:

- Full tenant exports can be many tens of GBs depending on retention window and activity; we typically deliver via chunked CSV/GZIP pieces.
- Legal hold requests prevent automated deletion; if Financio requests a hold, we can tag records and provide an export snapshot, but we need a signed scope and retention window to proceed operationally.
- For cross-border concerns: our default export endpoint for this account is in us-west; if they require EU residency we need an additional handoff plan.

I attached a tiny sample (first 48 hours) so they can validate schema.

Next steps: can you confirm the exact export window Financio wants and whether they need checksums + manifest per chunk? Also want to know if they will accept SFTP push or prefer an encrypted cloud bucket share.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: audit_log_sample_chunk_1.csv (CSV, 120KB)]

From: Alex Lopez <alex.lopez@financio.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit log export: initial scope and constraints

Marissa —

Thanks for the note and the sample. Financio confirms:

- We need 24 months of audit/access logs for our tenant (all actions, admin/login events).
- Delivery: prefer encrypted S3 (us-west) with per-file SHA256 checksums and a manifest file.
- Legal hold: our legal team will place a hold for an ongoing investigation; we need assurance that exported records will not be auto-deleted on your side for the hold duration.

We can sign scope later today if you send over the export template/manifest format.

Regards,
Alex Lopez
Head of IT Security, Financio Inc.
security-contact@financio.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Lopez <alex.lopez@financio.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit log export: initial scope and constraints

Marissa / Karthik —

Operational notes from infra: we can generate a chunked export with the following guarantees:

- Chunk size: default 10GB compressed per object; we can reduce to 2GB if the customer prefers smaller pieces.
- Manifest: JSON manifest with chunk filenames, start/end timestamps, record counts, and SHA256 checksums. We can also include a running offset token for resume.
- Legal hold: we will create a hold flag at the tenant level that prevents automatic TTL-based deletion. Hold can be time-bound or indefinite; we need a signed request from the customer to activate.
- SLA for delivery: 5 business days from signed scope for a 24-month export for a single tenant (typical load). If they request EU egress or air-gapped transfer, add 3–7 days.

I attached the internal playbook and a manifest example. Marissa, can you confirm whether Financio will provide an S3 bucket with a cross-account role or they want Redwood to push to an SFTP endpoint?

-Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Cloud Ops Engineer — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: export_playbook_chunking_v2.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Lopez <alex.lopez@financio.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit log export: initial scope and constraints

Alex —

Thanks Ben — appreciate the details. Alex, Financio providing an S3 bucket with a cross-account role is best for speed. A couple clarifications on legal hold and downstream deletion:

- We will mark the tenant with a legal_hold flag which prevents our retention engine from deleting records older than the retention window. However, customers retain the right to request deletion; legal holds override deletion only on our backend policy until the hold is removed.
- Export copies we provide are treated as data egress artifacts — removing the hold on the source tenant does not automatically delete copies we already delivered to the customer's bucket. If Financio wants Redwood to also purge exported copies on de-escalation, we need an explicit orchestration request and access to the destination to perform purge operations (or a signed attestation from them that they will handle destination lifecycle).

Proposed operational checklist for Financio to sign:
1) Confirm CSV schema acceptance (see sample).
2) Provide cross-account S3 ARN + role.
3) Sign legal-hold activation request (we'll then prevent TTL deletion).
4) Confirm whether Redwood is authorized to purge exported copies on hold release (yes/no).

If you confirm the above, we'll queue the export.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Thanks — we reviewed and are aligned on the checklist. Quick answers:

1) Schema: accepted.
2) S3: will provision cross-account role by EOD tomorrow and share ARN.
3) Legal hold: legal will sign and send the request once we receive a short export statement from Redwood confirming the hold block prevents your TTL deletion.
4) Purge of exported copies: Financio prefers to manage the destination lifecycle. We do not want Redwood to purge our S3 objects.

Please send over the short export statement we can attach to legal's request. Also, Ben — can you confirm the manifest format (we'll use it to validate checksums)?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Alex
